short: GLI factors are five-fingered C2H2 zinc-finger proteins that read the nine-base site GACCACCCA and form the transcriptional output of the Hedgehog pathway. Humans have three canonical members: GLI1, an activator that is itself a Hedgehog target gene, and GLI2 and GLI3, which are made as full-length activators but are partially degraded into N-terminal repressors when Hedgehog signaling is off. The related GLIS1, GLIS2 and GLIS3 proteins read a close variant, GACCCCCCAC. Binding is monomeric and the informative bases are concentrated at the 3' end of the site, which fingers four and five contact directly. GLI sites control limb and neural-tube patterning, and pathway mutations cause polydactyly syndromes, basal cell carcinoma and SHH-subgroup medulloblastoma.
long:
## The factors

Three canonical human GLI proteins, GLI1, GLI2 and GLI3, are the vertebrate counterparts of
Drosophila Cubitus interruptus. Each carries five tandem C2H2 zinc fingers and binds DNA as a
monomer. GLI2 and GLI3 are bifunctional: an N-terminal repressor domain and a C-terminal
activation domain flank the finger array, and limited proteolysis removes the activation domain to
leave a repressor [PMID:10693759,39576500]. GLI1 lacks the N-terminal repressor region and is a dedicated activator; because
GLI1 transcription is itself induced by Hedgehog signaling, GLI1 mRNA is widely used as a pathway
readout. GLI2 and GLI3 are broadly expressed during development, whereas GLI1 accumulates only
where the pathway is active.

The GLIS subfamily, GLIS1, GLIS2 and GLIS3, is the nearest relative: Kruppel-like proteins with
five fingers whose DNA-binding domains are close enough to GLI that their motifs cluster together [PMID:14500813],
but whose expression is largely non-overlapping (GLIS3 in thyroid, pancreatic islets and kidney,
GLIS2 in kidney, GLIS1 in a restricted set of tissues and in oocytes). A fourth entry, GLI4
(ZNF767P), is annotated as a family member but the matrices assigned to it in these databases do
not resemble a GLI site; treat it separately.

## The motif

The consensus GACCACCCA was defined by selecting genomic fragments bound by recombinant GLI: the
protein protected 23-24 bases at each site, and all recovered sites contained the same nine-base
core [PMID:2105456]. The crystal structure of the five GLI fingers on a high-affinity site explains the shape of
the information content. Finger one makes no DNA contact; fingers two through five wrap into the
major groove without the strictly periodic geometry of Zif268; and fingers four and five make
extensive base contacts across a conserved nine-base-pair stretch whose conformation is
intermediate between B- and A-form DNA [PMID:8378770]. The consequence is that the 3' half of the site
(reverse-strand TGGGTGGTC) carries most of the specificity while the 5' flank is tolerant.

Systematic affinity measurements of every single substitution show a wide dynamic range [PMID:16413481], and
reporter assays with natural promoters show that many low-affinity variants still drive strong
activation at moderate GLI concentrations [PMID:20070907]. So "non-consensus" GLI sites are functional, and a
strict consensus search under-counts real elements. The GLIS paralogues prefer GACCCCCCAC, with the
central ACC replaced by CCC [PMID:23332764]; the databases keep GLI and GLIS as separate matrices, but their
cross-similarity is high enough that only strong matches can be assigned to one subfamily. The data
consensus here, GACCACCCACgdcG, is the same core with a weakly informative 3' extension.

## Where it acts

GLI binding is mostly at distal enhancers rather than core promoters, and GLI sites are not a
CpG-island feature. ChIP of GLI activators in Hedgehog-responsive mouse neural tissue recovers on
the order of a thousand high-confidence regions, enriched at known pathway components (Ptch1, Gli1,
Hhip) and at patterning genes (Foxa2, Nkx2-2), with the motif recovered de novo [PMID:17442700]. Because the
informative core is nine bases with degenerate flanks, exact matches occur tens of thousands of
times in the human genome and the great majority are never occupied. Occupancy tracks pathway
activity and chromatin: the same sequence is silent in tissue where GLI2 and GLI3 are not
stabilized. Frequent neighbors in Hedgehog-responsive enhancers include SOX2, FOXA2 and NKX
factors, and ZIC proteins, which bind an overlapping sequence and can physically associate with GLI
zinc fingers.

## Biology and disease

Hedgehog ligand binding to PTCH1 relieves inhibition of SMO, which blocks the phosphorylation of
GLI2 and GLI3 by PKA, GSK3 and CK1 and thereby blocks their processing [PMID:39576500]. In the unstimulated state
GLI3 is converted into a truncated repressor, GLI3R; in the developing limb this produces a graded
anterior-to-posterior distribution of repressor that patterns the digits [PMID:10693759]. SUFU sequesters GLI
proteins and opposes the pathway.

Gli2-null mice lack a floor plate and show reduced Shh responses [PMID:9636069]; Gli1-null mice are viable and
only reveal defects in combination with a Gli2 mutation [PMID:10725236], consistent with GLI2 being the principal
activator and GLI1 an amplifier. Truncating GLI3 mutations cause Greig cephalopolysyndactyly
syndrome, while frameshifts in the middle third of the gene, which leave a repressor-like product,
cause Pallister-Hall syndrome [PMID:20301619,15739154]. GLI1 was originally cloned as an amplified, highly expressed gene in
a human glioma [PMID:3563490], and Hedgehog-driven tumors (basal cell carcinoma, SHH-subgroup medulloblastoma)
signal through GLI even when the initiating lesion is in PTCH1 or SMO [PMID:39576500]. On the GLIS side, biallelic
GLIS3 loss causes neonatal diabetes with congenital hypothyroidism [PMID:16715098], GLIS2 (NPHP7) loss causes
nephronophthisis [PMID:17618285], and GLIS1 improves the efficiency of somatic-cell reprogramming [PMID:21654807].

## Reading a hit

A GACCACCCA match identifies the GLI/GLIS class and nothing finer. GLI1, GLI2 and GLI3 have
effectively the same matrix, so no sequence argument distinguishes them; assignment to a member
comes from expression or ChIP data. More importantly, a hit does not tell you the sign of the
output, because GLI3R binds the same site as GLI2 full-length activator. With nine informative
bases the site is common enough to occur by chance in any few-kilobase window, so an isolated match
is weak evidence; conservation, open chromatin in a Hedgehog-responsive tissue, and proximity to
other pathway targets all help. Conversely, the functional importance of low-affinity variants
means absence of a consensus match does not exclude GLI regulation. In HOCOMOCO, the GLI2 and GLI3
models carry in vitro support (HT-SELEX and methyl-SELEX, grade A), whereas the GLI1 model is
ChIP-only at grade C; the GLI4 entries are ChIP-only and do not look like a GLI site at all.
caveats: A hit tells you "GLI/GLIS", never which paralogue and never whether the factor present is an activator or the GLI3 repressor. The nine-base core occurs frequently by chance, so isolated matches carry little weight without conservation or Hedgehog-responsive chromatin. GLI and GLIS matrices differ at only one or two central positions, so weak matches cannot be assigned to a subfamily. Low-affinity, non-consensus sites are demonstrably functional, so consensus searching both over-calls inert sites and misses real ones. The GLI4/ZNF767P matrices in these databases are ChIP-derived and unlike the GLI site; the Vierstra archetype carrying that motif is named GLI but groups poorly with the rest of the family.

timeline.finding: GLI is identified as a gene amplified more than 50-fold and highly expressed in a malignant glioma; its sequence predicts a zinc-finger protein.
timeline.methods: Gene amplification analysis, cDNA cloning, chromosomal mapping
timeline.open: Whether the protein bound DNA, and what sequence, was unknown.

timeline.finding: Binding-site selection from total human DNA with a recombinant GLI protein recovers three sites, each footprinted over 23-24 bases and each containing GACCACCCA.
timeline.methods: Genomic binding-site selection with PCR recovery, DNase I footprinting
timeline.open: The consensus rested on three natural sites; which positions were essential was not tested.

timeline.finding: Crystal structure of the five GLI fingers on a high-affinity site: finger 1 makes no DNA contact and fingers 4 and 5 make most base contacts across a nine-base-pair stretch, explaining why the 3' half of the site carries most of the specificity.
timeline.open: A single site was solved; how variant sites are tolerated was not addressed.

timeline.finding: Hedgehog-regulated, PKA-dependent processing of GLI3 produces a repressor distributed as an anterior-posterior gradient in the limb, so the same site can receive activator or repressor input.
timeline.methods: Biochemical analysis of GLI3 processing in chick and mouse limb; human syndrome and chick talpid2 mutants
timeline.open: How an enhancer distinguishes activator from repressor bound to the same sequence.

timeline.finding: High-throughput affinity measurements for GLI1-3 across single-substitution variants of the site give a quantitative specificity model, used to predict Hedgehog-responsive enhancers genome-wide.
timeline.methods: High-throughput in vitro binding-affinity assay, computational enhancer prediction, transgenic mouse reporters
timeline.open: Many natural GLI target sites scored as low affinity, raising the question of whether they were functional.

timeline.finding: ChIP of an epitope-tagged GLI activator in differentiating mouse neural progenitors identifies direct targets, including enhancers of Nkx2-2 and Nkx2-1, confirmed in transgenic embryos.
timeline.methods: ChIP-chip on targeted genomic tiling arrays, transgenic reporter assays
timeline.open: Coverage was limited to candidate loci rather than the whole genome.

timeline.finding: Reporters carrying every single substitution of the site show that many low-affinity variants activate strongly at moderate GLI concentration, revising the view that only consensus GACCACCCA sites are functional.
timeline.methods: Luciferase reporters in the PTCH1 promoter context, natural non-consensus promoters
timeline.open: Reporter assays in cultured cells do not show how affinity is used to read the Hedgehog gradient in tissue.

timeline.finding: A large HT-SELEX survey of human transcription factors gives the GLIS paralogues a GACCCCCCAC site, which differs from the GLI1-3 site GACCACCCA at the central ACC.

open: Why many functional Hedgehog-responsive enhancers use low-affinity GLI sites is unresolved: one view is that weak sites restrict the response to cells with high activator levels and so sharpen the readout of the Hedgehog gradient, the other that weak sites are simply sufficient at moderate GLI concentration and are not selected against.

Whether GLI activators and the GLI3 repressor occupy the same genomic sites in vivo, or whether some sites are read preferentially by one form, is not settled; the three proteins share one matrix in vitro, so any difference would have to come from chromatin, partners or site arrangement.

Whether GLI4 binds a GLI-type site at all is unknown: the only matrices assigned to it are ChIP-derived and share a TGGCATTCAAGGCC consensus unrelated to GACCACCCA, and a Vierstra archetype labeled GLI carries the same sequence.
